conviction_note: The quarter is a large headline beat that Roche published on Oct 22: its Japan pharma sales rose 49% at constant rates in Q3. About 1pt of Roche group growth (~CHF 150-180m, roughly JPY 30bn) is an ERP shipment-timing effect that Roche flagged itself, and the stock has rallied 14.6% from its Oct 9 low (+4.3% since the Roche release), so the beat is largely priced. What the release adds is the decision on the FY guide (core OP JPY 670bn, IFIS consensus ~3-4% above it): Chugai raised at Q3 2024 and held at Q3 2025 despite 79% progress. With a crowded margin long (19.7x) and two straight good prints sold off (-15.8%, -7.7%), the measurements lean very slightly negative: findings sum -0.1, scaled -0.27 from abs 4.5 and p_up 47.

findings.finding: Roche's 9M 2026 release puts Japan Pharma sales at CHF 2,352m (H1 1,360m), so Q3 is CHF 992m against 714m a year earlier, +49% at CER per Roche's quarterly table. On the H1 ratio (Roche Japan ~1.06x Chugai domestic plus other overseas supply), that is about JPY 180-190bn against JPY 123bn in Q3 2025 and JPY 136bn in Q2 2026. Roche attributes it to 'product supply to third parties', product growth (Lunsumio, Hemlibra, Polivy, Elevidys, Vabysmo) and a positive ERP timing effect worth about 1pt of group Q3 growth (7% vs 6% excl. ERP), roughly CHF 150-180m or JPY 30bn. Chugai's Q3 revenue therefore likely lands near JPY 370-395bn against ~350bn implied by the unrevised IFIS FY consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: revenue +11.5%, OP +16% (kabutan 'good results') sold -15.8% on 'material exhaustion' (Foundayo scripts that day). Q2 2026: OP +17% YoY but Q2 core OP ~5% below consensus, -7.66%. Q3 2025 (Roche data a day before) -3.06%. Beats have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The stock rose +2.7% on Oct 23 (kabutan/Fisco: 'Roche sales figures still being valued') and +1.5% on Oct 26. What may not be priced is the headline size against a consensus that IFIS shows unchanged for four weeks: kabutan's 'surprise results' screens and retail read the raw YoY number, not the ERP-adjusted one. If it were fully priced, the IFIS FY revenue consensus would have moved after Oct 22, and it has not. It is sized small because Roche flagged the ERP effect, so any sell-side model has stripped it out.

ERP effect in JP', Japan Q3 +49% CER) is the same issuer's document, so it counts once. kabutan 2026-10-22 (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=4519&b=n202610220932) reports the same Roche disclosure plus the stock's reaction.

findings.finding: The FY guide decision is the item the release adds. H1 core OP was JPY 329.1bn, 49.1% of the JPY 670bn plan against 43.6% a year earlier. With the Q3 above, 9M is likely ~77-79% of plan, so the plan implies a Q4 core OP well below Q4 2025's JPY 172.7bn, and IFIS consensus already sits ~3-4% above the plan. Chugai's own record cuts both ways: it raised at Q3 2024 (stock +14.35%) and held at Q3 2025 with 9M core OP at 79% of a JPY 570bn plan (FY landed at 623bn), when the stock fell ~3%. The ERP pull-forward reverses in Q4, which gives management a ready reason to hold again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024 upward revision beyond expectations: +14.35% (kabutan 2024-10-28 'stock jumps more than 10% on a larger-than-expected upgrade'). Q3 2025 hold at 79% progress: -3.06% (baseline estimated date). The plan was held at Q1 and Q2 2026, with reactions of -15.8% and -7.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether the plan moves is unknown until the release, and both outcomes have precedent. The street at ~3-4% above plan means a hold is a mild disappointment rather than a relief (the reverse of the case where the street is below plan), and a raise only to consensus level is neutral. If the market were pricing a confident raise, the IFIS FY consensus would have moved up after Roche's data, and it has not. Sized only slightly negative because the precedent is one year each way.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print on a crowded leveraged long: margin ratio 19.69x, a 14.6% rally from the Oct 9 close (6019) to the Oct 26 close (6897), and a reaction function that sold the last two good prints hard (Q1 'good results but material exhaustion' -15.8%, Q2 'double-digit OP growth but material exhaustion' -7.7%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-27 -15.83% and 2026-07-27 -7.66%, both described by kabutan/MINKABU as 材料出尽くし (sell the news) after good headline numbers.
findings.why_not_priced: This partly IS the price: the baseline's priced lean is -0.98, mostly the margin overhang. What it adds is this name's specific habit of selling good prints, which neither the lean nor the run-up control captures. If the overhang had cleared, the margin ratio would have fallen and the stock would not have rallied into the date.

findings.finding: Q2's miss was attributed to weak Hemlibra exports to Roche and low Foundayo royalties. In Q3, Roche's Hemlibra sales held at about CHF 1,258m for the quarter (9M 3,750m vs H1 2,492m, +12% CER YTD), Japan Hemlibra was +20%, and Roche raised its 2026 Hemlibra outlook to high-single-digit growth. That supports the Roche royalty line (JPY 68.4bn in H1, plan 178.5bn for FY), although the export volume to Roche follows Roche's ordering and is not visible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: Hemlibra exports to Roche flat (JPY 63.2bn) and below expectations, cited by Fisco in the -7.66% reaction (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=4519&b=n202607270355).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced since Oct 22. Royalty income is mechanical on Roche's in-market sales, so a raised Hemlibra outlook flows to Chugai's royalties, while the Q2 narrative was that this line disappointed. A proxy, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Same Roche Q3 document set as finding 1 (different line: Hemlibra product sales, not the Japan region), so the documents overlap. Not double-counted: finding 1 is domestic sales, this is royalties.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-29 Roche returned the GYM329 (emugrobart) licence after Chugai ended its obesity development; Roche had estimated JPY 380-570bn of peak sales for it. The stock fell 4.2% to a low that day and has since recovered past it.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced: the stock absorbed it on Sept 29 and has since rallied. It is filed only because the Q3 release or call could carry a pipeline-write-off line or an R&D re-prioritisation comment. No intangible for it is visible in the H1 IFRS-to-core reconciliation (H1 intangible adjustment ~JPY 1.2bn).

outside_window.finding: Lilly's Q3 2026 results (Foundayo / orforglipron sales, which set Chugai's royalty narrative) are expected around end-October, after Chugai's window closes on Oct 28.

Returns: dividend forecast 132 yen (66/66), core payout target ~45%, so a core EPS raise could lift it; no buyback history with a 60% Roche parent. baseline_tension: The findings mostly agree with the priced lean (-0.98, margin overhang) and run against the run-up (+6.7%, which the free control reads as negative), so they add little to it. The strongest positive the release could carry is a FY core OP/revenue raise with a dividend increase, as at Q3 2024 (+14%). I looked: no pre-filed revision exists, the 9M progress makes a raise plausible, and Chugai held in the same position a year ago. So the sign is close to a coin flip and the net is near zero.
